name: automation
description: A commit written by automation on a schedule or a trigger — fleet-sync, a status mirror, a bot — never by someone choosing what to say. A commit that adds or changes automation is ci or tooling.

name: bootstrap
description: The first commit of a repository, or the scaffold of a whole new component where nothing stood before. After that first landing every change has a more specific kind.

name: revert
description: Undo an earlier commit, restoring what stood before it. The preset already reads git's own `Revert "…"` subject; write this when you word the subject yourself.

name: removal
description: Take something away — code, files, a feature, a repository — and leave nothing in its place. Carries `!` (or `%`) whenever anything outside the repository could have referenced what left. Relocating is move; undoing a commit is revert.

name: move
description: Rename or relocate — files, paths, repositories, where a task lives — with the content itself unchanged. If what moves also changes shape, name the change instead.

name: security
description: The commit exists because of a security or permission finding: least-privilege permissions, secrets and tokens, a vulnerability-driven version bump. The finding wins over whatever the diff touches.

name: license
description: The LICENSE file, and nothing else.

name: ignore
description: .gitignore, and untracking what should never have been tracked.

name: assets
description: Media and other binary or generated artifacts committed as they are: images, sounds, fonts, a rendered diagram. Test fixtures are tests; records the code reads are data.

name: data
description: Records rather than code: the furrow board, a snapshot, seed data, a dataset the code reads. Changing how records are read or written is code and takes that kind.

name: tests
description: Tests and their fixtures, nothing that ships: add, extend, deflake, restructure. A test that lands alongside a fix belongs to the fix.

name: ci
description: What runs on a CI runner: .github/workflows, actions, the reusables and their callers, and repairing a build that broke there.

name: tooling
description: Scripts and hooks a developer runs locally: build.sh, check.sh, scripts/, git hooks, the nix dev shell. If it runs on the runner it is ci.

name: config
description: Configuration files the tools read: glyph.toml, linter and formatter config, dependabot.yml, dotfiles, app settings. Workflows are ci; build scripts are tooling.

name: distribution
description: How the built artifact reaches a machine: goreleaser, a Homebrew cask or tap, a nix flake, install.sh, code signing, an app bundle.

name: dependency
description: A version move of something external — up, down, added, removed, or pinned: go.mod, Package.swift, a `uses:` tag, an install-action version. The direction is not a kind.

name: release
description: The act of releasing: a promotion to 1.0 (`%`), lockstep version pins cut ahead of a tag, publishing or deploying. Moving a dependency's version is dependency.

name: docs
description: Prose a reader reads: README, docs/, CLAUDE.md, design notes, code comments. Text the product shows its user is ui.

name: ui
description: What the user sees and reads in the product: layout, colour, type, spacing, wording on screen, in --help and in error messages. A new capability is feature; wrong output is fix.

name: accessibility
description: Accessibility: VoiceOver and other assistive technology, Reduce Motion, contrast, keyboard reachability.

name: performance
description: Faster or leaner with the same observable result. If the result was also wrong, it is fix.

name: fix
description: Behaviour was wrong — against the spec, the docs, or plain intent — and now is right. Severity is not a kind: a hotfix and a one-liner are both fix.

name: feature
description: A capability that did not exist: a new command, flag, key, screen, option, integration. Changing what an existing capability does is fix (it was wrong) or refactor (same behaviour).

name: refactor
description: Restructure code with observable behaviour unchanged: move logic, split or merge types, change internal contracts. Surface-only changes are polish.

name: polish
description: Code hygiene with neither behaviour nor structure changed: formatting, lint and compiler warnings, naming, comment tidy, typos in code.

name: checkpoint
description: A step that is not coherent on its own and lands only inside a pull request that finishes it. Always `=`; the squash keeps the PR title.
